title: Tin whistle
summary: The tin whistle is a small six-hole duct flute with a plain metal tube and a beak mouthpiece, at home in the traditional music of Ireland. The air runs through a narrow channel onto an edge, so the sound is bright and clear and the fingers can run fast.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. Eight notes of the scale are lit down the tube.
Each strike shows the fingering of that note and a band of breath runs from the beak to it.
Strike close to the beat; a long note swells slowly.
rules: A phrase is a line of notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It is the first instrument of many players, light enough to carry anywhere, and its tunes run through sessions and dances.
credits: Tradition: the tin whistle; phrases written for this game
